nodes.label: A5 Sign-In Screen
nodes.rationale: Returning-member entry surface for the Steigenberger Hotel Doha 'Privilege Guest' app. Headline 'Welcome back' / 'Sign in with your mobile number'. Layout is a three-band phone screen: branded hero header (image placeholder + STEIGENBERGER wordmark + PRIVILEGE GUEST eyebrow), a raised rounded card holding the single credential field and primary CTA, then a secondary text link and a legal footer pinned to the bottom. Dark luxury palette (near-black #2a211d ground, champagne/gold #e8d3a0 accent) with a single filled gold pill as the only primary action, so the screen has exactly one obvious next step.

nodes.label: Mobile Number Field (+974)
nodes.source_location: credential card, split input with country-code gutter
nodes.rationale: Split control: fixed '+974' Qatar dial-code segment divided by a hairline rule from the editable local number ('3312 3456' shown as sample data). The dial code is pinned rather than a picker because the property is single-market (Doha), which removes a country selector from the critical path. This is the only credential collected - there is no email or password field anywhere on the screen.

nodes.label: Send Passcode Action
nodes.source_location: credential card, primary gold pill below the number field
nodes.rationale: Primary CTA. Labelled by its effect ('Send passcode') rather than a generic 'Continue', so the user is told a one-time code is about to arrive by SMS before they leave the screen. Triggers the transition to the A6 passcode screen.

nodes.label: Have an Invitation Code? Entry Point
nodes.source_location: below the credential card, gold text link with caret
nodes.rationale: Secondary route out of sign-in into first-time activation. Rendered as a low-emphasis gold text link with a caret, deliberately outside the credential card, so enrolment never competes visually with the returning-user path. Its presence on the sign-in screen means sign-in is treated as the default surface and activation as the exception.

nodes.label: Terms and Privacy Consent Notice
nodes.rationale: 'By continuing you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.' Implicit consent bound to the CTA rather than an explicit checkbox, which keeps the form to a single field but ties acceptance to the act of requesting a passcode.

nodes.label: Privilege Guest Programme Eyebrow
nodes.source_location: base of the hero header band, gold letterspaced caps
nodes.rationale: Gold letterspaced 'PRIVILEGE GUEST' caps sit beneath the hotel lockup, naming the loyalty programme as a sub-brand of the property rather than a separate brand. Same treatment repeats on A6; on A7 the slot is taken by the 'ACTIVATE MEMBERSHIP' eyebrow, so the position acts as a per-screen context label.

nodes.label: Hero Header Image Placeholder (Lobby / Evening)
nodes.source_location: top band, dashed rectangle x 11.6-280.4, y 12.1-183.6
nodes.rationale: Dashed-outline rectangle labelled 'IMAGE PLACEHOLDER' with the art direction brief 'LOBBY - EVENING' typeset inside it. The hero photograph is unresolved in the design; the slot and its brief are specified while the asset is pending. Repeats identically across A5, A6 and A7, so the header is a shared component rather than per-screen art.

nodes.label: Passwordless Phone-Number Authentication
nodes.rationale: The flow carries no password field, no email field and no 'forgot password' affordance anywhere across A5/A6/A7. Identity is the mobile number and the proof is a transient SMS passcode. Trade-off accepted: guests never manage a credential and there is no reset path to support, at the cost of a hard dependency on SMS deliverability - which is why A6 carries both a resend timer and a call-the-front-desk fallback.
